question: Should memory-wiki vault isolation be solved through generic `agents.list[].plugins` overrides, a memory-wiki-owned per-agent vault contract, or context-aware vault path templating?
rationale: This changes durable plugin config, sensitive memory boundaries, and possibly SecretRef/lifecycle semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product and security contract.

options.title: Design generic agent-scoped plugin config
options.body: Add a shared per-agent plugin config contract with precedence, SecretRef handling, schema validation, restart behavior, and memory-wiki adoption on top of it.

options.title: Keep config global; add memory-wiki vault routing
options.body: Leave `plugins.entries` global and add a memory-wiki-specific per-agent vault map or safe template contract for vault operations only.

options.title: Defer and document separate gateways
options.body: Keep memory-wiki as a single-vault plugin for now and document separate gateway processes as the supported hard-isolation workaround.

recommendation.title: Design generic agent-scoped plugin config
recommendation.body: Add a shared per-agent plugin config contract with precedence, SecretRef handling, schema validation, restart behavior, and memory-wiki adoption on top of it.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available owner signal because the choice spans plugin config, security-sensitive memory boundaries, and recent memory-wiki/config history.
